purpose: Trusted Business Report v2 — G28-A grounding ≥ 0.85 on real data. The 11:34 UTC 2026-09-21 showcase run (snapshot 136a49f5, groundedShare 0.82 = 18/22) left four residual patterns: (1) a conversion rate the CRO derived from two register numbers ('5 of 182 ≈ 2.7%'), (2) a statutory fee the CLO remembered ('$290 ASIC fee', '~$250 per class') and a checklist contradiction, (3) a content-plan cadence the CMO wrote as a fact ('3–5 articles, each 2,000+ words'), (4) a market-entity subset the CMO derived from the anchor ('roughly 1,400 entities … 30–40 accounts'). Each case pins: the bare number stays uncited (never mis-cited to a knowledge row), the declared-estimate form ('we estimate … [unevidenced]', EN and VI) clears the gate, and a figure that IS in a platform-knowledge row (ASIC / IP Australia fee band, sector entity count) is auto-cited to that row. Ids are the pipeline's stable calc| ids.

evidenceRows.label: ASIC and IP Australia fees: annual review fee band, trade mark fee per class (platform knowledge)
evidenceRows.value: ASIC annual review fee (proprietary company, s 345A Corporations Act 2001): A$321 (FY2024-25) to A$329 (FY2025-26) a year, indexed each 1 July — the current-year figure is at https://asic.gov.au/for-business/payments-fees-and-invoices/asic-fees/fees-for-commonly-lodged-documents/; a special-purpose company pays a reduced fee (about A$67). Late payment fee: about A$96 within one month, about A$401 after one month. The annual statement is issued on the registration anniversary and the fee is due within 2 months. IP Australia trade mark application fee: A$250–A$550 per class (A$250 for a standard online filing with a pick-list specification, up to A$550 with a custom specification) — https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/trade-marks/understanding-trade-marks/trade-mark-costs. Two classes (e.g. class 36 financial services + class 42 software) therefore cost A$500–A$1,100 to file.
